description: Human Rights Watch publizierte am 1. Mai 2019 den 68-seitigen Bericht "China's Algorithms of Repression: Reverse Engineering a Xinjiang Police Mass Surveillance App". Zwischen Januar 2018 und Februar 2019 hatten HRW-Forschende eine Mobile-App reverse engineered, die Polizei in Xinjiang mit der Integrated Joint Operations Platform (IJOP) verbindet. IJOP aggregiert Daten zu Telefon, ID-Karten, Strom-/Tankstellen-Nutzung und flaggt "Mikro-Auffaelligkeiten" wie SIM-Wechsel, Stromverbrauchs-Abweichungen oder Verlassen registrierter Wohnorte zur Untersuchung. Eine 2020 erfolgte Auswertung zeigte: Das System hat ueber Tausende Uyguren in arbitraere Internierung versetzt.

description_en: Human Rights Watch published its 68-page report "China's Algorithms of Repression: Reverse Engineering a Xinjiang Police Mass Surveillance App" on 1 May 2019. Between January 2018 and February 2019 HRW researchers reverse-engineered a mobile app linking Xinjiang police to the Integrated Joint Operations Platform (IJOP). IJOP aggregates data on phones, ID cards, electricity and petrol consumption and flags "micro-clues" such as SIM swaps, electricity-use deviations or leaving registered residence for investigation. A 2020 follow-up analysis showed: the system has channelled thousands of Uyghurs into arbitrary detention.
